body:
**Background**
- He caddied from age 11 at Brae Burn Country Club and caddied for Fidelity's president, D. George Sullivan. In college he bought **Flying Tiger** air freight with about $1,000 (around $7/share) on the idea that "air cargo was going to be a thing of the future," and it was his first tenbagger — [PBS Frontline interview](https://www.pbs.org/wgbh/pages/frontline/shows/betting/pros/lynch.html) [VERIFIED-PRIMARY]; [CapexCat](https://capexcat.substack.com/p/peter-lynch-buy-what-you-know) [SECONDARY]
- He was a Fidelity summer intern in 1966 (about 75 applicants for 3 spots), an analyst from 1969 at $16,000/yr, and director of research in 1974 at age 30 — [CapexCat](https://capexcat.substack.com/p/peter-lynch-buy-what-you-know) [SECONDARY]

**Fund size and performance**
- "When I took over in May of 1977, the fund was $20 million… When I left Magellan Fund, it was 14 billion" — [PBS Frontline](https://www.pbs.org/wgbh/pages/frontline/shows/betting/pros/lynch.html) [VERIFIED-PRIMARY]. CRSP shows $22M at end-1976, and Lynch's own count elsewhere is about $18M. Assets were $107M at end-1981 and passed $1B in April 1983. The fund was closed to new investors until it opened to the public in 1981, when it had about $100M — [CapexCat](https://capexcat.substack.com/p/peter-lynch-buy-what-you-know); [CBS MoneyWatch](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/lessons-from-a-great-fund-managers-record)
- **Returns:** 29.2%/yr vs. the market's 15.5% (CRSP, June 1977–May 1990). It beat the market in 108 of 156 months, with about 7.9%/yr alpha — [CapexCat](https://capexcat.substack.com/p/peter-lynch-buy-what-you-know). CBS gives **26.4%/yr vs. the S&P 500's 13.3%** for 1977–1990. The sources differ by method and period — [CBS MoneyWatch 2010](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/lessons-from-a-great-fund-managers-record); [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Lynch)
- **The small early base mattered:** the best years came while the fund was under $100M and closed to new money. It only opened to the public in 1981 at about $100M. In 1986 alone it took in $2.3B of new money on a $4.1B base — [CBS MoneyWatch](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/lessons-from-a-great-fund-managers-record)

body:
`case_study:reliance-capital-adag` | 2021-11-29 | tickers: RELCAPITAL, RCOM, RPOWER, RHFL | confidence: verified

The Anil Dhirubhai Ambani group (ADAG) was valued near Rs 1 lakh cr+ at the Jan 2008 peak (Reliance Power's Rs 450 IPO was oversubscribed ~70x and fell below issue on listing). Over 2008-2020 group stocks (RCom, Reliance Capital, Reliance Infra, Reliance Home Finance) lost 95-99%. Reliance Capital peaked ~Rs 2,700+ (Jan 2008, unverified exact) and traded in single digits by 2020. RBI superseded its board on 29 Nov 2021; Hinduja's IIHL won with a ~Rs 9,650 cr plan (NCLT Feb 2024; completed Mar 2025), wiping equity. SEBI (Aug 2024) banned Anil Ambani and 24 entities for 5 years and fined him Rs 25 cr for diverting Reliance Home Finance money via 'general purpose corporate loans' to group-linked entities with weak financials. Visible flags: (1) GPCL loans from RHFL/RCap rising from ~Rs 900 cr to ~Rs 7,900 cr in a year to thinly capitalised borrowers; (2) auditor PwC resigned from RCap and RHFL in 2019 citing concerns it couldn't resolve; (3) near-100% promoter pledges; (4) RCom's 2G-era debt and failed asset sales (Jio spectrum deal blocked); (5) rating downgrades to D in 2019; (6) intra-group cross-holdings and guarantees. Lesson: lending subsidiaries of conglomerates lend to the conglomerate; auditor resignation with stated reasons is near-certain disqualifier.

**Lesson:** Group NBFCs fund the group; auditor exit = sell
**Spotted early by:** PwC (auditor); SEBI forensic review
**Links:** illustrates -> `insight:auditor-exit-signal`, illustrates -> `insight:promoter-pledge-group-contagion`, illustrates -> `insight:lender-blowup-signals`, illustrates -> `insight:disqualifiers`
**Sources:** <https://www.business-standard.com/companies/news/rhfl-fund-diversion-case-5-year-market-ban-for-anil-ambani-24-others-124082300983_1.html> ; <https://www.businesstoday.in/amp/latest/corporate/story/acquisition-of-rcap-completed-by-indusind-international-holdings-ashok-hinduja-468399-2025-03-18> ; <https://www.deccanherald.com/business/companies/nclt-approves-hinduja-group-firm-indusind-international-holdings-resolution-plan-for-reliance-capital-2911775> ; <https://www.business-standard.com/amp/article/markets/2g-scam-unitech-rcom-wipe-out-97-shareholder-wealth-in-10-years-117122100260_1.html>

title: watchlist › Watchlist — every stock analysed

body:
For every flag, good or bad, fill: flag | context questions | clearing evidence (external) | confirming evidence | verdict | what changes my mind | review date. Rules from `insight:flag-override-template`:
- A management explanation alone keeps a flag OPEN.
- Three or more open soft flags means no position without a written variant view.
- Hard disqualifiers (fraud signals, auditor exit on denied information, related-party diversion, fake cash) cannot be overridden.
- Include **"looks good" flags**. Inflated KPIs and definitional flattery mislead more often than ugly numbers.

---
title: deep_dive_protocol › Synthesis (L7): the override table

body:
- **Choose sites to test hypotheses.** Use a mature unit, a new unit in a new geography, and a different format or near-cannibalising unit. Visit off-peak and peak.
- **Count before you talk:** queues, bills per hour, footfall, staff and guards, facings, prices of a fixed basket. Numbers first, opinions second.
- **Talk to five constituencies:** staff, store or plant manager, customers, neighbours/competitors, and a supplier, landlord or driver. Ask about pay, tenure, rent, trips, and switching.
- **Ethics:** identify yourself honestly if asked. Never pay for or solicit confidential or unpublished price-sensitive information (that is insider-information risk). No recordings without consent.
- **Repeat the fixed price basket quarterly.** It is a cheap time series nobody else has.
- **B2B version (v1.1).** Use three visits: (A) an OEM or channel partner and two competitor dealers in the same city, (B) the company's dealer workshop or parts counter, (C) end-users and installers.
  - Count: price sheets *by product node* (same nodes every quarter), price-hike dates and percentages by component, lead times by platform, service bays and jobs, and a fixed basket of 5 spare parts (genuine vs will-fit).
  - Ask end-users the engineering ratio that sizes demand (e.g. DG MW per IT MW).
- **Output:** a "surprises vs model" list. Each model estimate is marked confirmed, contradicted or no read.

title: deep_dive_protocol › Scuttlebutt (L6) design rules

body:
```bash
sudo apt update
sudo apt install -y python3 poppler-utils sqlite3 git curl
sudo timedatectl set-timezone Asia/Kolkata      # so cron times below are IST
git clone https://github.com/aditya-bad/fein.git ~/fein   # private repo: use a GitHub token or deploy key,
                                                          # or just copy tools/detectors/ onto the Pi
mkdir -p ~/fein-data
echo 'export FEIN_DATA=$HOME/fein-data' >> ~/.bashrc
```

`poppler-utils` (`pdftotext`) is not needed by the detectors; it is there for reading the filing
PDFs that alerts link to. `curl` is preinstalled on Raspberry Pi OS; BSE only answers over HTTP/2,
which Python's urllib cannot do, so `collect.py` calls `curl --http2` for BSE.

Check that everything works, then build a first baseline:

```bash
cd ~/fein/tools/detectors
python3 collect.py --selftest      # live, tiny fetch of every source, writes nothing
python3 detect.py --selftest       # live Indo Tech pledge check + offline rule tests
python3 collect.py                 # yesterday -> today
python3 detect.py
```

The pledge rules compare two snapshots, so they only start firing from the second evening.

Useful options:

```bash
python3 collect.py --from 2026-11-18 --to 2026-11-20   # backfill a range
python3 collect.py --only pledges,deals                # subset: announcements,bse,insider,sast,deals,pledges
python3 collect.py --no-bse                            # skip the BSE backup feed
python3 detect.py --from 2026-11-18 --to 2026-11-20 --all   # re-list alerts already seen
```

Exit codes: `collect.py` returns 1 only if every step failed (each step is logged and recorded in
the `runs` table); `detect.py` returns 0 unless it crashes. Only one copy of `collect.py` runs at a
time (lock file in `logs/`).

body:
- 2026-11-21: pre-registration above written; scripts in `tools/backtests/solvency_us/` (s1 candidates from float
  frames → s2 SEC submissions + reduced companyfacts → s3 flags → s4 EDGAR events → s5 tickers + Yahoo → s6 analysis).
  4,843 candidate CIKs. Fetch interrupted by a usage limit at 1,162 firms; resumed 2026-11-22 from cache.
  Implementation notes fixed before outcomes: the float fact is taken from the T-10-K's own accession (some filers
  tag the float with a wrong date, e.g. Sanmina FY2015); S4 requires payouts > 0 (otherwise every cash burner fires).
- 2026-11-22, **deviation found on audit of EDGAR events (before any flag-vs-outcome statistic was run):** the
  pre-registered O_delist (8-K 3.01 + Form 25/15 + no merger) was dominated by *voluntary exchange transfers*
  (Workday, Garmin, Xerox, Expeditors, Palo Alto… moving Nasdaq↔NYSE file exactly that pattern). Revised O_delist =
  the 3.01 8-K text shows a substantive listing-rule failure (deficiency / minimum bid / not in compliance / late
  filing / suspension; the item-heading boilerplate stripped; transfer language and pure governance-composition
  notices excluded) **and** a Form 25/15 on or after that notice in the window **and** no merger evidence
  (`s4b_item301_text.py`). Results under the as-registered definition are also reported (`O_fail_asreg`).

title: solvency_flags_us › Stage log

body:
- O_fail is understated for the 45% of rows without Yahoo history (they can fail only via EDGAR); price-based failure and
  winner counts are survivor-tilted. EDGAR events are not.
- 8-K item 1.03 is also filed for a subsidiary's bankruptcy; spot check of 30 found only real parent-level Chapter 11s.
- Float-based size is stale; current SIC; as-first-reported XBRL with tag fallbacks (custom tags → unknown/0; capex missing → 0).
- Same firm in up to 3 snapshots → CIK-clustered bootstrap; failures cluster in 2015–16 energy and 2020.
- The revised delisting definition is a post-audit deviation (19 vs 199 events); results under the as-registered version
  are lower but give the same verdicts (S1 2.07, S5 2.12; CIs > 1).
title: solvency_flags_us › Caveats

body:
Source rule: decision:solvency-flags-graded and lesson L24, from the pre-registered US test
(`research_notes/Backtests/solvency_flags_us.md`). In the US these flags roughly doubled the odds of failure
within 5 years but caught only 8-16% of failures. **Use: look harder and size smaller. Not a sell or short
signal, not protection.** The Indian adaptation below is UNTESTED on Indian outcomes until the
survivorship-free re-test (`research_notes/Universe/india_dead_companies_probe.md`) is run.

FY0 = latest fiscal year in screener's profit-and-loss table (consolidated; screener falls back to
standalone where there are no consolidated accounts, column `basis`). Balance sheet at the same date.

| flag | India definition | vs the US test |
|---|---|---|
| S1raw | net worth = Equity Capital + Reserves < 0 (minority interest not included) | same |
| S1 | S1raw, unless payout-driven: FCF > 0 and dividends paid over the last 3 years >= the deficit | US exempted *buyback*-driven negative equity. Indian buybacks are small and screener does not split them out, so only dividends count; the exemption should almost never fire |
| S2 | interest cover EBIT / interest < 1.5x, EBIT = Operating Profit - Depreciation + recurring Other Income (FY0 other income clipped to [0, its 3-year median]). Interest 0: not fired if borrowings < 5% of assets | US EBIT = operating income. Screener's Other Income carries one-off gains and losses (Vodafone Idea FY26: +Rs 59,292 cr from dues relief), so only its usual level counts; recurring treasury or regulatory income (NHPC) still counts |
| S2b | interest cover < 2.5x (India-adjusted variant: Indian rates are higher) | **untested; reported, never graded** |
| S3 | short-term borrowings > cash equivalents + 0.5 x CFO (screener Borrowings and Other Assets schedules) | Ind AS puts current maturities of long-term debt in short-term borrowings, matching US "debt current". Cash excludes liquid mutual funds (screener "Investments"), which Indian treasuries use a lot, so S3 is stricter than in the US |
| S4 | dividends paid > FCF and borrowings rose on the year | buybacks not counted (not separable) |
| S5 | >= 2 of S1-S4 | same |
| S5b | >= 2 of S1, S2b, S3, S4 | **untested variant** |

Banks, NBFCs / financial institutions, housing finance, insurers and margin-funding brokers are excluded
(`status=financial_alm`): borrowing is their inventory and they need an asset-liability-maturity test.
FY0 older than 550 days = `stale_fy` (company may have stopped filing). Graded red = S1 or S5.

```bash
python3 solvency_screen.py --selftest              # offline flag checks
python3 solvency_screen.py --sample 150 --seed 7   # validation sample
python3 solvency_screen.py                         # full universe, ~1,550 names x 4 requests, ~2.5 h
python3 solvency_screen.py --symbols IDEA,VEDL --no-db
```

title: lazy_prices_us_v2 › 3. Survivorship audit (EDGAR events after the filing date; firm-years without usable prices)

body:
- **Primary:** 13-week excess return = `r13 − cA13` (size-matched controls), from the event file.
- **P(halving):** the lowest weekly close in (entry, entry + 52 weeks] ≤ 0.5 × the entry close (weekly series from the
  same price caches as the event file: v1 Yahoo daily → Friday weekly closes, with v1 split adjustment; screener
  weekly for MISSING firms). A firm whose series stops inside the window counts on what traded (halved or not); an
  event whose series ends because the data end (last close within 14 days of the latest date in the cache) before
  entry + 52 weeks − 7 days, without having halved, is dropped from this outcome (counted).
title: combined_avoid_india › Outcomes

body:
| Layer | Primary sources (in order of value per hour) |
|---|---|
| L1 | DRHP/RHP "Industry overview" (commissioned research such as RedSeer or CRISIL: biased but detailed); "Our Business" chapter; peer DRHPs |
| L2 | Annual-report notes (not the front half); screener.in (re-derive, never trust "Borrowings" or "ROCE" blindly); quarterly results; `tools/nse_fetch.py results` |
| L3 | DRHP KPIs (stores, area, payback, cohort data); investor presentations; call transcripts (`nse_fetch.py transcripts`); broker *analyst-meet* notes (they relay closed-door numbers) |
| L4 | **AR note "Other expenses"** (security, manpower, housekeeping, power, freight lines); **BRSR** (headcount, *% of employees at minimum wage*, median pay, attrition, energy GJ, water); state labour-department wage notifications; SERC tariff orders (power); freight indices; commodity prices |
| L5 | AR related-party note (Ind AS 24) by year; **Reg-44 voting results of AGMs/postal ballots (v1.4)**; **AGM-notice and postal-ballot material-RPT annexes (pricing formulas, royalty rate, sunset clause; v1.1)**; Form AOC-2; DRHP risk factors ("our Promoters provide us services…"); shareholding pattern; SAST/insider/pledge (`nse_fetch.py sast/insider/pledge`); block/bulk deals; ESOP grant intimations (Reg 30); AGM/postal-ballot notices (pay, strike prices); MCA filings of promoter entities |
| L4 (manufacturers, v1.1) | Materials ratio by quarter from results; commodity series (BigMint, SteelOrbis, Mysteel for pig iron and steel; LME for Cu/Al; freight indices); BRSR energy, water and waste plus *physical-output intensity*; regulatory notifications (CPCB, CAQM, NGT, BIS/QCO orders); SPCB consent-to-operate orders (permitted capacity) |
| L6 | Store/plant visits; B2B channel checks (OEM/dealer price sheets by product node, lead times, parts prices); GeM/railway/defence tender results; MCA filings of private channel partners and sister companies; job portals (AmbitionBox, Indeed, Naukri) for pay and attrition reviews; Google Maps (reviews, competitor distances); landlord/broker rent quotes; dealer and supplier calls; app-store reviews; quick-commerce price checks by PIN code |
| L7 | memdb `insight:flag-override-template`; our false-alarm case base (`--tag false-alarm`) |
